To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the crystalline complexes of PEG with lanthanoid(III) nitrates have been prepared and their structures determined; (b) the complexes of PEGs of low molecular weight are 1:1 complexes, while those of PEGs having molecular weight of more than 200 are 1:2; and (c) the stability of the complexes is in the order: La > Ce > Pr > Nd > Sm > Eu > Gd.
we have synthesized a series of lanthanoid complexes with the poly(ethylene oxide) derivatives and that the stability of the complexes decreases with increasing atomic number.

the crystalline complexes of lanthanoids with poly (oxyethylene), HO(CH2CH2)4H, and poly (oxyethylene)-dimethyl ether, CH3O(CHCH2O)5CH3, were prepared, characterized by X-ray powder diffraction, IR and NMR spectra, and thermal analysis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and structural characterization of lanthanoid complexes with poly(oxyethylene) ligands.

the synthesis of lanthanoid complexes of poly(oxyethylene) derivatives and with the study of the properties of the complexes, including the structure of the complexes, the stability of the complex and the thermal stability of the complex.
the preparation and properties of crystalline complexes of the type (CH3O(CH2-CH2O)2CH3)2Ln(NO3)2 (Ln = La, Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu) and (HO(CH2-CH20)nH)2Ln(NO2)3 (Ln = La to Lu, n=2, 3, 4, 6).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lanthanoids form complexes with these poly(oxyethylenes).
the complexes with n=3 and 6 are the most stable ones.
the lanthanoid ions are coordinated to the ether oxygen atom of the poly(ethylene oxide) unit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the poly (oxyethylene)s are good ligands for the lanthanoids.
the complexes of lanthanoid naphthenate, nitrate and acetate have the composition of [ligand]2[Ln(NO3)2(H2O)4].
a complex of poly (oxyethlene) with lanthanoids can be prepared by the method of crystallization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complexes have a 1:1 composition, which is in contrast to the 1:2 composition of the previously reported complexes.
the lanthanoids are not inert to the polyether ligands and that the polyether complexes may have potential applications in catalysis and materials science.
the poly(oxyethylene) derivatives are excellent ligands for preparing lanthanoid compounds.
